The *Susaṁvuta Sutta* (*Sekhiya* 5) is a training rule situated within the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Titled *Susaṁvuta* in Pali and rendered as "Being unrestrained" by Bhikkhu Sujato, the rule concerns proper comportment and self-restraint while in inhabited areas [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. All secondary literature passages retrieved under the designation "sk 5" are false matches referring to non-Vinaya treatises, notably the *Sāṁkhyakārikā* and the *Mahāyānasangraha*.

The rule is extensively paralleled across the canonical codes of early Buddhist schools [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Vinaya, exact counterparts exist in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk5*), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk5*), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bi-pm-sk5*), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Parivāra* (*Sekhiya* 5) [SuttaCentral]. Across other traditions, parallel rules are preserved in the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya (attested in Chinese translations and Sanskrit manuscript fragments), the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya (extant in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit), the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (Chinese), the Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda traditions (Sanskrit), and the Kāśyapīya Vinaya [SuttaCentral]. Internally within the Pali canon, text-reuse analysis shows 110 matching passages across 42 Pali texts, driven by the standardized, formulaic phrasing shared with numerous other *Sekhiya* rules, most notably *Sekhiya* 13, 15, 11, 14, and 26 [DharmaNexus].
